model_annotation: Figure 5 displays two line plots illustrating training dynamics for different model variants during training from scratch. The left plot, labeled (a) "Loss w.r.t steps", shows the training loss over steps for five methods: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), StrmLLM (n=128), SepLLM (n=64), and SepLLM (n=256). The x-axis represents the number of training steps on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 1000 with tick marks at intervals of 200. The y-axis represents the training loss on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. All lines are solid and marked with circular points. The Vanilla model starts with a loss of approximately 0.8 and decreases to about 0.1. StrmLLM (n=64) starts at approximately 0.75 and drops to about 0.15. StrmLLM (n=128) starts at approximately 0.7 and ends at about 0.15. SepLLM (n=64) begins at approximately 0.7 and ends at about 0.12. SepLLM (n=256) starts at approximately 0.7 and ends at about 0.11, showing the steepest decline and lowest final loss among the models. The right plot, labeled (b) "Loss Ratio w.r.t FLOPs", shows the ratio of the loss values of different methods to that of Vanilla with respect to FLOPs. The x-axis represents FLOPs on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^15 to 10^18 with tick marks at each order of magnitude. The y-axis represents the loss ratio on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The lines follow the same color and marker scheme as in plot (a). All lines start at a ratio of 1.0 at the lowest FLOPs and decrease as FLOPs increase. The SepLLM (n=256) line ends at approximately 0.47, indicating a 53% reduction in loss relative to Vanilla at the highest FLOPs, while the Vanilla line remains at 1.0. The other models show intermediate ratios, with SepLLM (n=64) ending at approximately 0.55.
